A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VisionTS study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original VisionTS forecasting results, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and runtime measurements in Section 4 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v2 retains original forecasting experiments and adds PF benchmark results and an analysis of image and time-series representations.

M1.justification: The segmentation, normalization, grayscale rendering, bilinear alignment, MAE reconstruction, and inverse forecasting pipeline remains unchanged. Zero-shot inference and layer-normalization-only fine-tuning are retained. Revised dataset-specific period values concern experimental settings.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluations on the PF suite, including Solar, Walmart, Istanbul Traffic, and Turkey Power, substantially extending the represented data and populations. Electricity and Weather also appear in this suite but overlap names already present. Despite the PF designation, the added evaluations assess point forecasting, not distribution forecasts.

E2.justification: The new PF comparison includes previously unevaluated TiDE and TFT baselines. The runtime comparator set is substantially revised: v1 Table 15 includes PatchTST and all three MOIRAI sizes; v2 Table 5 drops PatchTST and MOIRAI Small/Large and adds TimesFM and LLMTime (8B). Existing long-term and Monash forecasting comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported Monash periodicities change substantially: M4 Weekly changes from P=1 to 4 and M3 Other from 2 to 1, also changing context lengths under the retained P-dependent rule. The added PF protocol uses L=2000 and sMAPE, MASE, ND, and NRMSE. The new representation analysis samples 1,000 images and 300 examples per time-series dataset using a consistent mask.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Figure 6 add an exploratory t-SNE analysis asking whether MAE representations of images and time series overlap. Existing ablations, scaling studies, sensitivity plots, and forecasting case studies are retained. The runtime comparison removes the c=1.0 variant; the new main-text context-length figure redisplays existing analysis.

E5.justification: The reported runtime averaging count changes from 20 runs in v1 Appendix B.8 to 90 runs in v2 Section 4.2. Full-shot experiments still report three runs, and Appendix C.2 retains the same standard-deviation reporting. No new confidence intervals or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: v2 adds PF results, including VisionTS NRMSE values of 0.448 on Electricity and 0.975 on Solar. With revised Monash settings, normalized MAE changes from 0.714 to 0.729 while aggregate rank remains second; M4 Weekly MAE changes from 314.83 to 404.23. Runtime measurements and relative-speed findings are also revised. Matched long-term forecasting and ablation tables retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The forecasting definitions, normalization and alignment equations, and computational-complexity reasoning are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. Added hyperparameter search grids and empirical metrics do not introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The central claims about image-based zero-shot forecasting and effective minimal fine-tuning remain. v2 adds an introductory claim that image representations can bridge heterogeneous time-series representations, extending the explanatory contribution beyond v1's general similarity motivation.

C2.justification: The alignment-width explanation changes from input-period geometry to matching MAE's pretraining mask ratio. v2 interprets embedding overlap as supporting transfer and images bridging heterogeneous series. New Section 7 explicitly identifies the inability to use exogenous covariates or forecast distributions and proposes continual pretraining. Existing case-based failure interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly documents frequency-specific period search ranges and validation-based selection; Appendix B.5 supplies PF hyperparameters. Conversely, v1's long-term dataset counts, date ranges, and provenance descriptions are removed, although frequencies and periods remain. Code-access, hardware, and full-shot training disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Fu et al. (2024) on synthetic time-series data and metric references by Hyndman and Koehler (2006) and Yu et al. (2016). It also expands discussion of the already-cited Yang et al. (2024) vision-pretraining approach. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract, introduction, and methodological explanations, groups analyses into Section 4.2, creates a separate limitations section, and subdivides Appendix A. These are localized rewrites and reorganizations; much of the methodological and experimental prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 adds PF summary and full-result tables, the representation plot, and a main-text figure redisplaying four context-length panels. It reorganizes periodicity tables, removes the long-term dataset-statistics table, and moves the TimesFM/LLMTime and runtime comparisons from appendices into the main text. These substantially revise the arrangement of experimental displays; Appendix D's forecasting examples remain.

improvement.justification: v2 broadens validation through PF evaluations on data described as unseen by both VisionTS and MOIRAI, explains period selection, and states concrete capability limitations. These improve the paper's evidential scope and interpretability. The gains outweigh the loss of dataset statistics and provenance details, but remain incremental: the core method and most results are unchanged, and the new representation analysis provides exploratory rather than decisive mechanistic evidence.
